description: Multi-head attention forward. Q is [batch, heads, seqlen_q, head_dim]; K and V share seqlen_k.

heads_kv.description: KV head count. Equal to heads is MHA, 1 is MQA, anything between is GQA.

alignment.description: Which corner the causal diagonal is anchored at. Only a distinct problem where the mask is causal and seqlen_q < seqlen_k; the constraint below pins it to top_left everywhere else, so the sweep does not spend half its budget measuring each shape twice. An engine that serves one anchor and refuses the other is removed from a comparison by the corpus rather than by a measurement, which is why this is a declared axis rather than a fixed choice.

// regime_label: The populations a corpus is reported per, as RFC 0019.13 §11.2's regret table needs them.
Phase: decode is one query token against a cache and is memory bound on that cache;
prefill is the whole prompt at once and is compute bound on the score matrix. They are the
same operation and entirely different problems, which is why they are anchored as separate
archetypes rather than as one range over seqlen_q. Cross attention (more queries than keys)
draws its two sequences from different tensors, so it varies independently of the rest --
the constraint above excludes it today, and the clause stays so that lifting the constraint
does not silently file cross-attention under 'append'.
Grouping (mha/gqa/mqa) is the third facet: how many query heads share one KV head decides
how much of the KV cache a wavefront re-reads, which is the whole difference between a
decode that is bandwidth bound and one that is not. It is a label rather than a bucket
because what matters is heads_kv relative to heads, not its magnitude.
// kernel_catalog: How a descriptor pack's metadata reads back as a point. The pack names its fields whatever
the kernel author named them; this is the only place those spellings appear, so a new pack
vocabulary is a declaration edit rather than a code change. A descriptor missing any mapped
field carries no geometry and contributes nothing -- which is how pointwise_add and the
shipped tiled_attention are excluded without naming them anywhere.
A pack value with no entry under `enums` is skipped and counted, never guessed: a pack in
fp8 read as bf16 would produce a corpus of graphs the engine does not serve, labelled as
`constants` answers for a parameter the pack vocabulary has no field for at all. These
packs record `causal` without recording which corner the diagonal is anchored at, because
every kernel in them anchors it top-left; saying so here is what lets the builder resolve
an argument no descriptor supplies. A parameter mapped under `metadata` is refused here,
so a constant can never overwrite what a descriptor actually said.

graph_builder.// types: Operands carry the declared dtype; accumulation and the score matrix are fp32. Left to default, compute follows io and every fp16/bf16 graph is uniform half precision, which hip-kernel-provider's SdpaFwdPlanBuilder refuses outright ('Compute data type must be FLOAT') and the ingestor engines decline at graph_match -- a live-engine corpus then admits nothing, indistinguishable from naming an engine that does not exist.
graph_builder.// layout: BSHD: dims stay (B, H, S, D) and the layout lives in the strides, token-major, as the shipped bundles and the retired Python bundler wrote them. Not row-major: strides_of would give BHSD, and rocKE's dense kernels take no stride kernargs -- stride_q_tok is baked as Hq*D -- so their matcher (hasBshdStrides) declines every BHSD graph, and a live-engine corpus for rocKE comes out empty. AITER serves BSHD too, so this keeps both engines in the contest.
graph_builder.// scale: attnScale is stated, not left to the schema's optional: rocKE's dense matcher declines a graph with no attn_scale_value (the scale is a required f32 kernarg and guessing 1/sqrt(D) is what it refuses to do), so omitting it empties a rocKE corpus. 1/sqrt(head_dim) is the standard scale and what the shipped bundles carry.

// archetypes: Recorded transformer configurations (RFC 0019.13 §12.3). Decode and prefill are the same operation and different problems -- seqlen_q of 1 against a long cache is memory bound, and a square prefill is compute bound -- so each is anchored separately rather than left to a range over seqlen_q.
// neighbourhood: head_dim is absent on purpose: it takes one of a few values fixed by the model architecture, and an interpolated 96 or 112 is not a configuration anyone ships. seqlen_k mirrors seqlen_q at ratios >= 1, which keeps the declared seqlen_q <= seqlen_k relation satisfied by construction rather than by rejection.
// mixture: Same shares as conv_fwd; see the note there.
